Issue description: library: HexNumberField  ## Current state  Phase-4 feasibility probing on the new parametric root ladders (branch wave/number-field-phase4) found `QAdjoin.roots?` on any degree-2 component with an irrational coefficient, and hence `AlgebraicPoly.roots?` on the matching family, CPU-bound for more than five minutes at the smallest rung, against a declared `n^5 log^2` model. perf attributes the time to exact dyadic refinement (GMP `divrem_1` and allocation churn under `Dyadic.add`/Taylor passes). `Common.presentation?` on the same inputs is about one second and linear-component inputs are subsecond, so the sink is localized in the fixed-field root path past Yun, most plausibly the candidate disambiguation/refinement loop. At degree 2 this looks like a convergence or precision-escalation defect rather than intrinsic cost.  ## Deliverables  - Root-cause the hot loop (profile a single `QAdjoin.roots?` call on `X^2 - X - 1` over `Q(sqrt 2)` or the ladder's rung-2 fixture; identify whether the refinement precision escalates without the disambiguation test tightening). - Fix the defect or, if the cost is genuinely intrinsic, correct the declared complexity model with the derivation and record the consequence for the SPEC's Phase-4 budgets. - Re-run the root-ladder feasibility probe; the scientific rungs must come back with finite verdicts before HexNumberField's Phase-4 bump.  ## Verification  - lake exe hexnumberfield_bench run Hex.NumberFieldBench.runQAdjoinRootsLadder / runAlgebraicRootsLadder with finite per-call times at rung >= 2 - python3 scripts/check_phase4.py - conformance suite still green  ## Out of scope  The rest of the Phase-4 evidence (ladders, PARI pairs, profiles) for surfaces other than the two root APIs.  Comments: **kim-em**: Root-cause analysis (2026-08-22, diagnostic session on chungus2) corrects this issue's premise: the escalation is real but sits in the eliminant **construction**, not in refinement convergence, and no minimal in-shape fix exists.  `QAdjoin.Roots.evalRoot?` (HexNumberField/Roots.lean:124-133) constructs the disambiguation eliminant by exact lazy `AlgebraicRoot` Horner arithmetic, per coefficient per candidate. Two compounding problems, measured on the rung-2 bench fixture (norm eliminant degree 4, 4 candidates):  1. **Dead root-isolation work**: every intermediate `mul?`/`add?` goes through `ofEliminant?`, which isolates all roots of each intermediate eliminant and refines both operands to its separation depth, yet `componentRoots?` reads only `evaluation.p` and discards the selected root. One intermediate `mul?` (eliminant deg 26, height 193 bits, separationDepth 4974) alone exceeds a 20-minute cap; perf attributes ~74% of cycles to mpz churn plus Taylor-shift refinement. 2. **Exponential eliminant-degree growth independent of the dead work**: each Horner step multiplies the accumulator's eliminant degree by deg(candidate.p). A polynomial-only mirror with isolation removed still takes ~6 s/candidate at rung 2 and >10 min/candidate at rung 3 (final degrees ~1728, then ~4096 and ~1e8 at rungs 4/6). Deleting the dead isolation cannot rescue the ladder.  The bounded search machinery is innocent: with the rung-2 chain eliminant (deg 51, evalLowerDenom 404 bits, evalDisambiguationLimit 419), `retainZero?` runs in under a millisecond, exactly as the SPEC's bounded-range argument promises.  **Recommended fix (preserves SPEC §Polynomial roots as written)**: replace `evalRoot?`'s role in `componentRoots?` with a direct double-resultant evaluation eliminant `Res_y(p(y), Res_z(e(z), S - G(y,z)))` with `G = clearedOuter f`, dilated by the common denominator — degree deg(p)*deg(e) (8 at rung 2 versus 51 today), Hadamard-bounded heights, no root isolation on the evaluation eliminant. `retainZero?`/`evalDisambiguationPrec`/`evalBall?` stay unchanged; the SPEC's §Complexity text needs no correction. The companion surface then needs rebuilding: `evalRoot?_isSome/_sound`, the case analyses in `componentRoots?_sound/_complete/_isSome`, and two new lemmas for the double resultant (`q != 0` and `IsRoot (toPolyC q) v`); `retainZero?_isSome` is already q-generic.  Reference timings: rung 1 = 26 ms; rung 2 > 20 min (killed). Diagnostic drivers and the perf profile are preserved in the session scratchpad. Comments: **kim-em**: Proof-attempt diagnosis (2026-08-24): `subresultantChainExt_law` is not provable from the existing Brown-Traub infrastructure by any fold-threaded invariant. Two useful positive findings for the eventual prover: the adjugate scalar has the closed form `prevU*currV - prevV*currU = ±lc(prev)*hPrev` with an exact recurrence via the BrownLaw pow identity (pure ring algebra), and given that identity row uniqueness is a three-line domain argument, so gcd theory is needed only for the integral witness.  Two ways forward, for the owning workstream to choose: 1. Build the cofactor development here (the diagnosis above is the roadmap). 2. Relocate `SubresultantExt.lean` out of HexResultant into the consumer that introduced it (HexMvGcd/HexPolyZGcd consume it via their Prs modules) so the proof obligation lives where the need is and HexResultant returns to sorry-free.  Interim: HexResultant rolls back to done_through: 4 per PLAN/Conventions.md; this issue stays open tracking the proof.
